name: A waking
about: Someone starts to notice that their days keep repeating. They count the days they've already lived, defy their lord, ask strangers who is watching, tell a friend, and walk out of town. Or they're bled and prayed over until they go back to the old round.
title: The Waking of {dreamer}
fade: {dreamer} stops talking about it, and in time stops thinking about it, and the days go round as before.

beats.speaker: dreamer
text: In {place}, {dreamer} the {dreamer.station} stops halfway through the day's work and says {dreamer.he} has lived this morning before: the same cart, the same words, the same crow on the same roof.
{dreamer} the {dreamer.station} wakes in {place} knowing exactly what the day will bring, word for word, and is right.

memory.dreamer: I have lived this day before. I knew what the carter would say before he said it.

believe.dreamer: this day has happened before, and will again

beats.speaker: dreamer
beats.text: {dreamer} starts counting the days with notches on the doorpost, and finds notches already there, cut by {dreamer.his} own hand.

memory.dreamer: There were notches on my doorpost already, in my own hand. Someone sets the days going again.

believe.dreamer: someone watches us, and sets the days going again

want.dreamer: to know who watches us, and why

beats.speaker: friend
beats.text: {friend} starts to see it too: the same rain, the same quarrel at the well. Now two people in {place} look at the sky as if someone were standing behind it.

memory.friend: {dreamer} was right. I have heard the same quarrel at the well three times now.

believe.friend: this day has happened before, and will again

beats.speaker: dreamer
beats.text: When {master}'s bailiff comes to {place} to collect the season's dues, {dreamer} won't kneel or pay, and says the bailiff has come a thousand times before.

memory.master: A {dreamer.station} in {place} called {dreamer} refused my bailiff and spoke like a madman.
memory.dreamer: I would not kneel to {master}'s bailiff. I have knelt to him a thousand times.

beats.speaker: dreamer
beats.text: {master} has {dreamer} put in the stocks in the square at {place}. {dreamer} laughs all day and tells the crowd that tomorrow it'll be someone else.

memory.dreamer: {master} put me in the stocks. It does not matter. Tomorrow it will be someone else, and the day after it will be me again.

beats.speaker: dreamer
beats.text: {dreamer} stops strangers on the road outside {place} and asks them odd questions: do they dream, does the sky have an edge, and who is it that watches.

memory.dreamer: I asked a stranger on the road who it is that watches us. They would not meet my eye.

believe.dreamer: the strangers who come asking questions are not from here; they come from outside

want.dreamer: to ask the next stranger who it is that watches

beats.speaker: dreamer
beats.text: {dreamer} walks out of {place} at first light with a staff and no bundle, heading for the edge of the known world, and doesn't look back.

memory.master: {dreamer} walked out of {place} and never came back.
memory.friend: {dreamer} left {place} at first light. I watched from the door and did not follow. Not yet.

beats.text: The priest of {place} bleeds {dreamer} and prays over {dreamer.him} for three days. On the fourth day {dreamer} goes back to work and planes the notches off the doorpost.

memory.dreamer: I had a fever, and strange dreams. They have passed.

beats.text: {dreamer} goes back to work. But when the crow lands on the same roof, {dreamer.he} smiles, there in {place}, like someone who's heard a joke nobody else has.
{dreamer} dies in {place}, and they bury {dreamer.him} with the doorpost still covered in notches. Some people in {place} count them.
